extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large-scale multilingual read-speech dataset derived from LibriVox audiobooks, covering 8 languages, with transcriptions, language models, and baseline ASR models for speech research.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, pt, it, pl
extraction.citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. December 22, 2020.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created from LibriVox audiobook audio and corresponding text sources by downloading audiobooks in selected languages, downsampling audio, segmenting long recordings into 10-20 second clips using acoustic models, generating pseudo-labels, downloading or manually retrieving book texts, normalizing text, matching pseudo-labels to source text to retrieve transcripts, filtering candidates by WER, and creating train/dev/test splits with speaker and gender balancing.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some audiobook text sources could not be downloaded or were invalid, and some candidate labels were filtered out during transcript retrieval; this reduced the final training data relative to the available audiobook hours.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read-speech audiobook audio from LibriVox and source texts from websites including Project Gutenberg, archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, and other online book sources.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz and segmented into 10-20 second clips based on silence intervals. Source text was split into overlapping documents, aligned to pseudo-labels using TF-IDF retrieval and Smith-Waterman alignment, and candidate transcripts with WER greater than 40% were filtered out. Numbers, hyphens, and apostrophes were post-processed with alignment-based replacement and heuristics.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio was downsampled and segmented; text underwent NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters, removal of end-of-line hyphenation, and filtering to valid unicode characters for each language. Books with corrupted metadata or multiple speakers were removed, and only the latest version of duplicate books was kept.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts were first generated automatically by pseudo-label generation and transcript retrieval from source texts. For development and test sets, human transcribers then listened to the audio while viewing the transcript and corrected only clear and obvious errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports word error rate between generated transcripts and human-rated transcripts for dev and test sets across languages, and constrained human corrections to only clear and obvious errors to reduce bias.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Acoustic models using TDS convolutions with ASG loss, wav2letter@anywhere for streaming inference, beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model, TF-IDF similarity retrieval, and Smith-Waterman alignment.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker gender labels were assigned for dataset splitting; speaker information and authors were present in metadata; in-house training data used for segmentation models was de-identified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote open research in large-scale and multilingual ASR and can also support multilingual TTS research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is based on read audiobooks, English is the dominant language, and the authors attempted to balance gender in development and test sets. They also constrained human corrections to avoid introducing bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Automatic text extraction was challenging for non-English languages due to diverse domains and invalid links; transcript generation is imperfect and filtered by WER; number normalization is not solved generically and relies on pseudo-label alignment, which may itself be incorrect; Polish language model decoding is negatively affected by high OOV rate.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for speech research, especially ASR and TTS, and includes train, development, and test splits as well as limited-supervision subsets for low-resource training benchmarks.

description.evidence: This paper introduces Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) dataset, a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research. The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriV ox and consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages. Additionally, we provide Language Models (LM) and baseline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models and for all the languages in our dataset.
